record.original_question: In deriving lower bounds and asymptotic information for minimal logarithmic and Riesz energies on the sphere, are there resummation methods more efficient than the summation-by-parts and inner-product-expansion approach described here?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2 (Johann Brauchart). Are there other more efficient resummation methods?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $d\geq 2$, let $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:|x|=1\}$ denote the unit sphere with its normalized surface measure. For $N\geq 2$ and a parameter $s$, define the discrete Riesz $s$-energy of an $N$-point configuration $\omega_N=\{x_1,\dots,x_N\}\subset\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ by
$$E_s(\omega_N)=\sum_{i\neq j}\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|^s}\quad (s>0),\qquad E_{\log}(\omega_N)=\sum_{i\neq j}\log\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|}\quad (s=0),$$
and let $\mathcal{E}_s(N)=\min_{\omega_N}E_s(\omega_N)$ (and analogously $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(N)$) be the corresponding minimal energy.

A standard route to lower bounds and asymptotic expansions of $\mathcal{E}_s(N)$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(N)$ as $N\to\infty$ proceeds by expanding the kernel $|x-y|^{-s}$ (resp. $-\log|x-y|$) in a series of Gegenbauer (ultraspherical) polynomials, then applying summation by parts (Abel summation) together with positive-definiteness properties of the partial sums of the resulting inner-product expansion.

Problem: Construct resummation techniques applied to the Gegenbauer expansion of the Riesz and logarithmic kernels on $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ that yield strictly sharper lower bounds (or higher-order terms in the asymptotic expansion) for $\mathcal{E}_s(N)$ and $\mathcal{E}_{\log}(N)$ than those produced by the summation-by-parts and inner-product-expansion approach. Equivalently, determine whether more efficient resummation methods than summation by parts exist for this class of energy asymptotics.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is part of a recent open-problems collection. While substantial work exists on next-order asymptotics for minimal Riesz and logarithmic energies on spheres (Brauchart–Hardin–Saff conjectures, Bétermin–Sandier–Serfaty renormalized-energy methods, Lauritsen's recent results on the logarithmic sphere case), no source found provides a resummation technique improving systematically on summation by parts in the Gegenbauer expansion approach. The status is best classified as open.

status_evidence.title: The next-order term for optimal Riesz and logarithmic energy asymptotics on the sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Brauchart, Hardin and Saff survey known results and present estimates and conjectures for the next-order term in the asymptotics of the optimal logarithmic energy and Riesz s-energy of N points on the unit sphere.
status_evidence.claim: Conjectures on next-order asymptotic terms remain open, indicating the need for new resummation/analysis techniques.

status_evidence.title: Renormalized Energy and Asymptotic Expansion of Optimal Logarithmic Energy on the Sphere
status_evidence.snippet: An asymptotic expansion for the minimum Hamiltonian is proven using gamma-convergence (Sandier-Serfaty).
status_evidence.claim: Alternative methods (gamma-convergence) exist but do not directly improve the summation-by-parts resummation in the Gegenbauer expansion framework.
